rationale: The first turn correctly mentioned that washer-dryers use a trickle of cold water to condense moisture, but it framed this as a supply fault rather than plainly telling the customer it is normal. The second question ignored the customer's statement that the clothes come out dry. The final reply confirmed normality but was muddled: it referred to heat-pump tumble dryers, included the broken line 'the most likely cause is confirm the complaint is genuine failure', and asked yet another question the customer had already answered (clothes dry well). No part was recommended and there was no safety issue.
